newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania says IMF backs monetary policy change.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania says IMF backs monetary policy change.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank said on Friday it reached an agreement with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on some aspects of its plan to gradually dismantle the currency board regime.
"We agreed in the spheres of monetary policy and banking," Bank of Lithuania govenor Reinoldijus Sharkinas told Reuters after meeting with an IMF delegation.
A letter of intent which supplements and updates the original deal with the IMF under which Lithuania has access to credits is expected to be signed at the begining of next week.
The central bank plans gradually to scrap the currency board model while keeping national currency litas pegged to a dollar at four to one rate untill 1998.
The currency board was included in the last IMF agreement and has to stay in place until at least September this year.
Under a currency board regime, the central bank guarantees that it will have a specific ratio of foreign funds in reserve to back the amount of local currency in circulation at the peg.
The central bank on Thursday said it will be more active in the money markets and will begin repo and reverse repo transactions in four to six weeks' time.
